> Kimi-K3 on gfx950 merge queue (all drafts; they land one at a time in this order): 1 #44978 verify argmax + tuned bf16 rows · 2 #44979 MLA prefill · 3 #44980 streaming AttnRes · 4 #44981 MoE prefill · 5 #44982 KDA · 6 #44983 MLA decode prep · 7 #44984 MLA decode epilogue · 8 #44985 LL column tail · 9 #44986 fused all-reduce read · 10 #44987 fused route sort · 11 #44988 split MoE front + bank partials · 12 #44989 MLA q-norm + q_b. Replaces #44547-#44553.

## Motivation

Two gfx950 decode costs outside any model's kernels: greedy EAGLE verify takes `torch.argmax` over wide vocabularies
(163,840 for Kimi-K3), which reduces each row on one workgroup, and on ROCm the verify results then go out as three
rank-0 broadcasts; and `UnquantizedLinearMethod` sends bf16 shapes that aiter's merged tuned table has measured rows
for to the Triton a16w16 path instead.

## Modifications

- Greedy verify on gfx950 with a vocabulary of at least 32K: `topk1.split_argmax` (the draft top-1 kernels' split
  argmax + a finalize kernel; first-max tie order, NaN ranks below every finite logit). The three verify outputs are
  views of one int32 buffer, so the rank-0 broadcast is a single collective (other platforms keep their allocations
  and broadcasts).
- gfx950 bf16 linears whose shape has a measured row in aiter's tuned table (`"us"` in the config) go to `tgemm.mm`
  ahead of the Triton a16w16 path.

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup for every number below:** 8x MI350X (gfx950, 1000 W), Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE, bf16 attention) at TP8 with EAGLE3
(topk 1, 3 steps, 4 draft tokens), FP8 KV cache, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, aiter's K3 FlyDSL kernels
(`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1`), CUDA graphs for bs 1/2/4/8/16, and an aiter bf16 GEMM table with K3 rows re-tuned on this pod with HBM-resident weights
(`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_BF16`; not part of this PR, it belongs in aiter's model configs). EAGLE3 on K3 needs the
aux-capture commit of #43599, applied locally for these runs. Microbenchmarks rotate their weights through HBM.
Per-feature numbers were measured on the integration branch of this series as each piece landed (Oct 13-14,
earlier `main`). All branches of the series are on `main` 4eb606b2ae (2026-10-17); the kernel tests below ran on this
branch, and the end-to-end checkpoints on that `main` plus the queue up to each slot.

- `test_spec_topk1.py` (new case): equal maxima in different vocab splits resolve to the lowest index and a NaN logit
  does not win, at 1 / 4 / 64 rows of a 163,840 vocabulary. On MI350X: 7 passed (15 subtests).
- End to end: GSM8K 200 at each checkpoint of the queue, see below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Greedy verify argmax, 163,840 vocab x 4 rows: 55 -> 9 us; with the MLA split combine of #44983, C1 decode
  cycle 19.4 -> 19.1 ms.
- The tuned-row preference is not measured on its own; it ran in every K3 measurement of this series.

### End to end (queue checkpoints)

K3 server built from `main` 4eb606b2ae plus the queue up to each slot, with #43599's aux capture (and #41867 and
#41848 from slot 10 on, which apply only once #44987 is in); C1 decode on a 50K-token cached prefix (500 output tokens)
and GSM8K 200, EAGLE3 as above, measured 2026-10-17. These runs and the previous integration below also set `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_AUTO_KV_SPLITS=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH=128 SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 AITER_MLA_REDUCE_FLYDSL=1`. In bold: the first checkpoint that includes this PR.

| Queue up to | Adds | C1 decode cycle | GSM8K 200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **slot 5** | **#44978, #44979, #44980, #44981, #44982** | **21.6 ms\*** | **0.995** |
| slot 7 | #44983, #44984 | 19.4 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 9 | #44985, #44986 | 18.6 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 10 | #44987, #41867, #41848 | 16.7 ms | 0.985 |
| slot 11 | #44988 | 15.7 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 12 | #44989 | 15.6 ms | 0.990 |

\* The second of two runs; the first, right after start-up, measured 25.6 ms. The other rows average two runs.

The whole series, from the previous integration: the seven earlier drafts (#44547-#44553) merged on `main` b67785153a (this series'
code plus the two opt-in paths it drops, both off by default), with #43599's aux capture, #41867 and #41848; agentic
replay of lightseekorg/agentic-dataset SWE-smith conversations (multi-turn, ~50K-token cached prefixes, 500 output
tokens, greedy), EAGLE3 as above. TokenSpeed (7e2f1deb, same pod, same workload) for reference.

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SGLang, tok/s/user | 217.2 | 156.6 | 114.1 | 73.4 | 43.4 |
| TokenSpeed, tok/s/user | 188.1 | 129.5 | 86.1 | 59.7 | 35.5 |

786/786 requests OK. GSM8K 400: 0.9825 / accept length 3.619. Decode cycle C1 / C4 / C16: 15.8 / 23.2 / 38.9 ms;
agentic turn TTFT (50K cached + 1.9K new tokens) 230-248 ms; uncached 50K-token prefill 3.27 s. The slot-12
checkpoint's C1 cycle (15.6 ms) is in line with it.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

files.patch:
@@ -160,3 +160,62 @@ def draft_topk1_argmax_only(next_token_logits: torch.Tensor):
         device=next_token_logits.device,
     )
     return draft_topk1_postprocess(next_token_logits, scratch_positions)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _argmax_finalize_kernel(
+    partial_vals,
+    partial_indices,
+    out,
+    num_splits: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    vals = tl.load(
+        partial_vals + row * num_splits + offsets,
+        mask=offsets < num_splits,
+        other=-float("inf"),
+    )
+    split = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
+    tl.store(
+        out + row, tl.load(partial_indices + row * num_splits + split).to(tl.int64)
+    )
+
+
+def split_argmax(logits: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1) for wide vocab rows, split across CTAs.
+
+    Same first-max tie order; NaN logits rank below every finite value instead
+    of winning."""
+    assert logits.ndim == 2 and logits.stride(1) == 1
+    rows, vocab_size = logits.shape
+    out = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int64, device=logits.device)
+    if rows == 0:
+        return out
+    num_splits = triton.cdiv(vocab_size, _DRAFT_TOPK1_BLOCK)
+    partial_vals = torch.empty(
+        (rows, num_splits), dtype=torch.float32, device=logits.device
+    )
+    partial_indices = torch.empty(
+        (rows, num_splits), dtype=torch.int32, device=logits.device
+    )
+    _draft_topk1_partial_argmax_kernel[(rows, num_splits)](
+        logits,
+        partial_vals,
+        partial_indices,
+        logits.stride(0),
+        vocab_size,
+        num_splits,
+        BLOCK=_DRAFT_TOPK1_BLOCK,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    _argmax_finalize_kernel[(rows,)](
+        partial_vals,
+        partial_indices,
+        out,
+        num_splits,
+        BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(num_splits),
+        num_warps=1,
+    )
+    return out

+    )
+    return "us" in config
+

 def _prefer_triton_a16w16(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> bool:

     if x.dim() != 2 or weight.dim() != 2:

         )
 
+    def test_split_argmax_takes_the_first_max_across_splits(self):
+        """Equal maxima in different vocab splits resolve to the lowest index, as
+        in torch.argmax; a NaN ranks below every finite logit instead of winning."""
+        vocab_size = 163840
+        for rows, dtype in (
+            (1, torch.bfloat16),
+            (4, torch.float32),
+            (64, torch.bfloat16),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(rows=rows, dtype=dtype):
+                g = torch.Generator(device=self.device).manual_seed(rows)
+                logits = torch.randn(
+                    (rows, vocab_size), dtype=dtype, device=self.device, generator=g
+                )
+                logits[:, [3, 70000, 150000]] = 50.0
